title: How I split up my week for Natural Hypertrophy
summary: Overview of his weekly program: an 8-day body part split (bench, squat, arms, deadlift, each in a 'competition' and a 'volume' version) run six days a week with Sundays off. He never deloads and trains 2-3 hours a day. Because the 8-day cycle runs over 6-day weeks, some main lifts drop out of a given week, which gives his body and mind a built-in break.

claims.claim: His program has 8 distinct training days run in a rolling cycle, training 6 days a week (Monday to Saturday) with Sunday off.
Each week he does 3 upper body and 3 lower body days, but it is a body part split, not push/pull/legs or upper/lower.
He considers a well-built body part split the smartest way to train as a natural bodybuilder.
Monday is always an upper day: either arm-dominant (biceps first, then forearms, shoulders, triceps) or chest-dominant (chest, then shoulders, triceps, a little biceps, no forearms).
His four session templates rotate bench, squat, arms, deadlift, so upper and lower days alternate.
Each template has a 'competition' and a 'volume' version; the volume day doesn't have more volume or less weight, it just swaps in variations of the main lift so the body can rest.
His main deadlift day uses conventional deadlifts and the second uses snatch-grip deadlifts: still a pull from the floor, arguably harder, but a different stimulus that lets his body recover.
When he pulled conventional every time he deadlifted he got stronger but got injured; rotating variations lets him gain all year without breaks.
He never deloads and takes only one rest day a week.
His sessions last 2 hours at best and sometimes 3, six days a week, all year round.
People call his training too much or say it is impossible for a natural; he answers that it works for him.
He built up training time gradually: at first he couldn't train 10 minutes, then 40 minutes, 1 hour, 2 hours; now a 1-hour session doesn't feel like a workout.
He spends long hours in the gym partly because he loves being there.

Running an 8-day program over 6-day weeks means two sessions drop out each week, so every few weeks he skips back squats or conventional deadlifts; this rests body and mind, and the next exposure gives PRs and more volume.
In weeks without back squats he still trains legs with safety squat bar squats and front squats.
